title: Listen to God, Not to Substitutes

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The nations you will dispossess listen to those who practice sorcery or divination. But as for you, the Lord your God has not permitted you to do so. - Deut 18:14 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God draws a sharp line between His people and the surrounding nations. Those nations listened to sorcerers and diviners, straining to hear guidance from shadowy sources. But God says of His people, "the Lord your God has not permitted you to do so." They were not to live like that, because they had something infinitely better, God Himself speaking to them.

What a contrast. The nations were left grasping at omens and spells, never sure, always anxious, trying to piece together the future from unreliable signs. God's people did not need any of that. They had the living God who spoke clearly and truthfully to them.

The same is gloriously true for us. We do not need to consult horoscopes, psychics, or any other substitute, because God has spoken to us fully and finally in His Son and through His Word (Heb 1:1-2). Why would we strain to hear whispers from unreliable sources when the God of all truth has spoken plainly? The world around us may still run after every kind of spiritual substitute, but we are called to be different, listening to God. His Word is trustworthy, His guidance is sure, and His Spirit leads us. Are you listening to God's clear voice in Scripture, or are you tempted by the unreliable substitutes the world offers?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What "substitutes" for God's voice tempt you?
2. Do you treat Scripture as God's trustworthy voice?
3. How can you grow in listening to God more attentively?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that You have spoken clearly through Your Word and Your Son. Help me listen to You and reject every unreliable substitute. Amen.
